script:
This is the New Saint Croix Union. Wednesday's biography is Michael Funk, Superintendent of Stillwater Area Public Schools.

Michael Funk grew up in Rochester. He earned a bachelor's degree in government from St. John's University in 1988 and a master's in education from the University of St. Thomas in 1994. He earned a doctorate in educational policy and administration from the University of Minnesota in 2004 and a master's in strategic studies from the U.S. Army War College in 2011.

He taught high school social studies at Dover-Eyota. He served as a high school principal in Pepin, Wisconsin. He was superintendent of the Bird Island-Olivia-Lake Lillian School District for four years. He became superintendent of Albert Lea Area Schools in 2009. The Minnesota Association of School Administrators named him 2022 Minnesota Superintendent of the Year.

He served 30 years in the Minnesota Army National Guard and retired in 2018 as a colonel. He commanded an infantry battalion in Kosovo in 2007 and 2008. In 2018 he was chief of the joint staff and oversaw security operations for Minnesota National Guard members during Super Bowl LII.

He and his wife Anne have been married more than 26 years. They have three daughters. The family moved to Stillwater in the summer of 2022.

On April 8, 2022, the Stillwater Area School Board selected him as the lone finalist for superintendent by a unanimous vote and offered him the job. He accepted. On April 19 the board approved a three-year contract. He began July 1, 2022.

At a staff kickoff he said his three core beliefs as a leader are expect the best, do the right thing, and do what is best for kids. He has said he wants the district to be great for staff, students, and communities, and that excellence is not easy but is a tremendous feeling when achieved. He has said the students, staff, and community deserve stable leadership, and that he has done his homework on what has transpired here.
